name: Suar
title: Chieftain of the tribe of Simeon
summary: Suar was the father of Selumiel, who served as leader and chieftain of the tribe of Simeon during Israel's journey through the wilderness. Suar is mentioned in connection with the census and the organization of the tribes at Mount Sinai. He belonged to the tribe of Simeon and played an indirect role through his son's leadership among the generation that wandered in the desert.

keyEvents.title: Selumiel Appointed as Tribal Chieftain
keyEvents.description: Suar's son Selumiel was appointed leader of the tribe of Simeon when God commanded Moses to organize the tribes of Israel.

keyEvents.title: The Census in the Wilderness
keyEvents.description: Selumiel, son of Suar, led the census of the tribe of Simeon, which numbered 59,300 men fit for battle.

keyEvents.title: Camp Arrangement Around the Tabernacle
keyEvents.description: The tribe of Simeon, under the leadership of Selumiel son of Suar, was stationed on the south side of the tabernacle together with the camp of Reuben.

keyEvents.title: Dedication Offering at the Tabernacle
keyEvents.description: Selumiel, son of Zuar, presented his offering on the fifth day during the dedication of the altar at the tabernacle.

keyEvents.title: Leader of Simeon's army
keyEvents.description: Selumiel, son of Zuar, was appointed leader over the military division of the tribe of Simeon when Israel broke camp.
